These petitions are filed by the respective appellants under Section 389(1) of the Code of Crimi
nal Procedure, 1973.
Following are the details of each petition.
Sl. No
. Crl.Appeal No. Crl.M.A. Nos. Filed by which accused 2.

All the petitioners were tried on a charge under Sections 143 147, 148, 294(b), 506(ii), 324, 326,
307 read with 149 of the Indian penal Code, 1860.
They were convicted for the offences under Sections 143, 147, 148, 324, 326, 307 read with 149 of the IPC.
The period of sentence the petitioners have to undergo in terms of the Crl.Appeal No.2006 of 2023 & Crl. Appeal Nos.61 and 54 of 2024 impugned judgment is 8 years of rigorous imprisonment.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the respective petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. Objections are filed by the 1 st respondent to all petitions.
It is contended that the prosecution has proved beyond doubt the charges levelled against the petitioners.

Considering the serious injuries inflicted to the victims and the threat posed to the injured even after the conviction, release of the petitioners on bail will adversely affect the safety and security of the injured.
Accordingly, the petitions are sought to be dismissed.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners were falsely implicated in the case on account of political rivalry, and the evidence brought on record is insufficient to prove the complicity of any of the petitioners.
Having gone through the judgment and considering the submissions on either side, the said contention is not liable to be accepted at this stage.
Crl.Appeal No.2006 of 2023 & Crl. Appeal Nos.61 and 54 of 2024 6.
The petitioners were convicted on 15.12.2023.
They have been in jail since the said date.

The learned counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on Shinde Gosai v. State of Gujarat [1999 (4) SCC 421], in order to contend that when a convicted person is sentenced to a fixed term of sentence, his plea for suspension of execution of the sentence shall be considered liberally.

8. The accusation against the accused Nos.8 and 9 in the aforesaid cases are also very serious.
Considering their criminal antecedents, I am of the view that they are not entitled to be released on bail by suspending the sentence.
In the said circumstances, Crl.M.A. No.1/2024 in Crl. Appeal Crl.Appeal No.2006 of 2023 & Crl. Appeal Nos.61 and 54 of 2024 No.54/2024 insofar as accused Nos.8 and 9 are concerned, is dismissed.
The said petition concerning accused Nos.5 and 6 is allowed.
9. Crl.M.A. No.1/2023 in Crl. Appeal No.2006/2023 and Crl.M.A. No.1/2024 in Crl.
Appeal No.61/2024 are allowed as follows:
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to apply before this Court for cancellation of the suspension of sentence.

P.G. AJITHKUMAR, JUDGE SMF 15-03-2024 /True Copy/

opennyai_summary.decision:
All the petitioners were tried on a charge under Sections 143 147, 148, 294(b), 506(ii), 324, 326,
307 read with 149 of the Indian penal Code, 1860.
The period of sentence the petitioners have to undergo in terms of the Crl.Appeal No.2006 of 2023 & Crl. Appeal Nos.61 and 54 of 2024 impugned judgment is 8 years of rigorous imprisonment.
Accordingly, the petitions are sought to be dismissed.
Having gone through the judgment and considering the submissions on either side, the said contention is not liable to be accepted at this stage.
The petitioners were convicted on 15.12.2023.
In that view of the matter, sentence imposed on the petitioners can be suspended except insofar as the persons who have serious criminal antecedents.
In the said circumstances, Crl.M.A. No.1/2024 in Crl. Appeal Crl.Appeal No.2006 of 2023 & Crl. Appeal Nos.61 and 54 of 2024 No.54/2024 insofar as accused Nos.8 and 9 are concerned, is dismissed.
The said petition concerning accused Nos.5 and 6 is allowed.
Appeal No.61/2024 are allowed as follows:
Execution of the sentence imposed on accused Nos.1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 is accordingly suspended and granted bail on their executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only), with two solvent sureties for the like amount each, to the satisfaction of the trial court, subject to the following conditions:

In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to apply before this Court for cancellation of the suspension of sentence.
